chunks: Shurays al-Wābishī informed me, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, the Greatest Name of Allah is made up of seventy-three letters. Asif had only one letter from it, and he spoke by it, so the earth between him and the throne of Bilqīs was swallowed up until he took hold of the throne with his hand. Then the earth returned as it had been, quicker than the blink of an eye.

And with us are seventy-two letters of the Greatest Name, while one letter is with Allah, the Exalted; He has kept it exclusively with Himself in the knowledge of the unseen that is with Him. There is no might and no power except by Allah, the All-High, the All-Great.

key_terms.آصَفَ: Asif, the figure who possessed one letter of the Greatest Name
key_terms.اسْمَ اللَّهِ الْأَعْظَمَ: the Greatest Name of Allah, a supreme divine name associated here with extraordinary effect
key_terms.سَرِيرِ بِلْقِيسَ: the throne of Bilqis, referenced as being brought miraculously
key_terms.عِلْمِ الْغَيْبِ: the knowledge of the unseen, which Allah uniquely retains in full
key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: a declaration that all power and ability belong only to Allah

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام say about the Greatest Name of Allah and the knowledge of the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the ism al-aʿẓam consists of seventy-three letters and that Āṣaf used one of them to bring the throne of Bilqīs instantly. It further declares that the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام possess seventy-two of these letters, while one remains exclusively with Allah تعالى in His unseen knowledge. The narration highlights both divine power and the special knowledge granted to the Imams عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad,f rom Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl who said, 
‘Shureys Al-Sabishy informed be, from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Magnificent Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is upon seventy three letters, and rather it was with Asif (Bik Barkhiya, successor<sup>as</sup> Suleyman<sup>as</sup>). So he<sup>as</sup> spoke with it, and the land which was between him<sup>as</sup> and the throne of Bilquis submerged to the extent that he<sup>as</sup> grabbed the throne by his<sup>as</sup> hand. Then the land returned just as it had been, quicker than the blink of an eye.

And we<sup>asws</sup>, with us<sup>asws</sup> are seventy two letters from the Magnificent Name, and one letter is in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted, which He<sup>azwj</sup> Accounts for the the Knowledge of the unseen. And there is neither Might nor Strength except with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Exalted, the Magnificent’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya and others have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who has said that Shurays al-Wabishi narrated from Jabir from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“The greatest name of Allah has seventy three letters. There was only of these letters. He spoke that one letter and land between him and throne of the Queen of Sheba (Bilqis) sunk down as such that he could reach her throne with his hand and the land returned to the original state. A number of our people has narrated from eye. Of the greatest name of Allah there are seventy two letters with us. Allah has kept one letter exclusively for Himself in the knowledge of the unseen. There is no means and no power except by the help of Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.”
